variants.user_notes: Connect only this iCESugar when programming: its programmer can't tell iCESugar boards apart, so the engine refuses when another board with the same USB IDs, such as an iCESugar-Pro, is connected.
variants.maintainer_notes: iCESugar boards share USB IDs and product name. The serial number's first 4 characters are the board ID, as icesprog's source reads it: 0700 iCESugar, 0710 iCESugar-Pro, 0720 iCESugar-nano. 0700 also seen in a real iCESugar v1.5's USB log.

sys_clk.user_notes: From the on-board iCELink's 12 MHz clock output.

source.ref: Pin test on a real iCESugar v1.5, 2026-11-22; github.com/wuxx/icesugar/issues/65

rgb_led.user_notes: Boards from newer batches swap green and blue from the schematic, as listed here; older ones follow the schematic (blue 39, green 41). If blinky lights blue instead of green, yours is an older one.
ai_hints: Wired to the FPGA's RGB LED driver pads: red RGB1, green RGB0, blue RGB2.
Newer batches' LED swaps green and blue from the schematic (blue 39, green 41).
Older boards follow the schematic; the maker plans to return to it (wuxx/icesugar#65).
Drive it through SB_RGBA_DRV, the iCE40 UltraPlus's RGB LED driver cell (sink only).

switches.user_notes: A 4-way DIP switch with pull-ups, S1 to S4 on pins 18 to 21, the same pins as PMOD4.

uart.user_notes: The on-board iCELink's USB serial port, over the USB-C cable. Also on PMOD1.

pmod1.user_notes: Shared: pins 2 and 8 with the UART, pins 1 and 7 with the micro-USB port.

source.ref: Pin test on a real iCESugar v1.5, 2026-11-22; MuseLab's iCESugar v1.5 pinout

pmod4.user_notes: A 2x6 header. One row: 3.3 V, GND, pins 18 to 21. The other: 3.3 V, GND, DIP switches S1 to S4.

requires.text: Remove PMOD4's 4 jumpers: as shipped, they connect pins 18 to 21 to DIP switches S1 to S4.

ai_hints: SPI flash, a W25Q64 (8 MB): CS 16, SCK 15, FPGA out 14, FPGA in 17, WP 12, HOLD 13.
Micro-USB port data: D+ on 10, D- on 9; 11 drives the 1.5k pull-up on D+.
